relevance_note: A 1982 metabolic study of three Tangier homozygotes with individual data in Table I ('Patients 1 and 2 represent the two original cases as described by Fredrickson et al. (1)'), plus three heterozygous relatives; no ABCA1 variant is described (pre-gene era), so the variants table is empty.
method_note: Rows built by a short Python script from my own reading; table rows quoted whole (Table I) or through the apoA-II cell (Table IV), checked against the tables. In-scope people: Tangier homozygotes patients 1-3 (text labels 'patient 1/2/3', matching Table I/IV 'Tangier homozygotes' rows 1, 2 a/b, 3 a/b), the two parents of patients 1 and 2 (sex not stated, labelled 'parent of patient 1' and 'parent of patient 1 2'; they are parents of both siblings) and the sister of patient 3. The paper does not say which of Table I 'Tangier heterozygotes' rows 1-3 (F 38, M 46, F 51) is which relative, so their per-row values (age, sex, lipids, Table IV kinetics) were not assigned to anyone. Rows a and b for patients 2 and 3 are not defined in the text (apparently two study occasions); age at last evaluation takes the later-age row b (26, 62); both rows are quoted as detail. Lab features for homozygotes come from the Results group statement naming 'Tangier homozygotes' (all three) with each person's table row as supporting detail; Table I HDL/VLDL columns lack a unit. Clinical features (enlarged orange tonsils, mild hepatosplenomegaly, lymphadenopathy, transient neuropathy, cholesterol-ester laden cells in skin and rectal mucosa) come from the Introduction about the 'two young siblings' of Fredrickson et al. (1), whom the Methods identify as patients 1 and 2; 'these patients' in the lipid-deposit sentence is taken to mean those two siblings (cites refs 1, 5-8). Heterozygote features: the parents 'did not share their clinical features' (recorded as one excluded row, not mapped to specific checklist items); heterozygote low HDL and normal LDL from statements naming 'Tangier heterozygotes'; the sister is assumed to be one of the '3 Tangier heterozygotes' because the parents and the sister are the only heterozygotes named; her disease label is not stated. Low apoA-I in heterozygotes is only in interleaved two-column text and was left not reported. No treatment, onset ages, consanguinity or vital status given. Contradictions/inconsistencies: 'Normal subjects (n = 28)' in Table I vs '26 normal male and female subjects' in Metabolic studies; Table I has two 'Tangier homozygotes (n = 3)' mean rows, the first apparently heterozygote means mislabelled; publication year not printed (received 1981, revised July 1982). The text is OCR with interleaved columns; spans were copied as they appear.
